edges.description: Ulcerated supraglottic lesions make swallowing painful.
The proliferative lesion presents as a laryngeal mass that resembles cancer.
A narrowed laryngeal lumen limits airflow on exertion.
Severe narrowing causes stridor and can become critical airway obstruction.
Critical narrowing obstructs the upper airway and may need a surgical airway.
Fibrosis, scar adhesion or vocal fold fixation leave persistent hoarseness in a minority of patients.
Scarring can stenose the larynx.
Infiltration and scarring around the cricoarytenoid region fix or paralyse a vocal fold.
Painful swallowing reduces food intake.
Smokers had lesions in more laryngeal sites than non-smokers; the mechanism is not established by the cited series.
Alcohol use is reported as a predisposing factor; the cited series do not establish how it acts.
Impaired host immunity predisposes to active tuberculosis including laryngeal disease; the cited sources do not tie it to a specific step.
